newsitem.title: UK: Major promises to aid probe into Conservative MP.
newsitem.headline: Major promises to aid probe into Conservative MP.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major, facing new embarassment over allegations of sleaze in his Conservative party, pledged on Thursday his government would cooperate fully with an investigation into a former minister's behaviour.
"I remain determined to maintain the reputation of parliament and to ensure that allegations of malpractice are investigated fully and impartially," Major said in a statement.

Former trade minister Neil Hamilton is to be probed by parliament's Commissioner For Standards, Sir Gordon Downey, following claims by Mohamed Al-Fayed, owner of London's Harrods store, that he paid him cash to table parliamentary questions.
Major published a letter he has written to Downey telling him: "I have made arrangements to ensure that you receive the government documents that are relevant to your investigation."
Fayed's original allegations caused Hamilton to issue a writ for libel against the Guardian newspaper which published them.
But on Monday, the day before the case was due to come to court, the former minister called off the case, paying the Guardian a nominal sum towards its legal costs.

Since then, the Guardian has printed fresh claims about Hamilton's connections with al-Fayed and with parliamentary lobbyist Ian Greer whom al-Fayed engaged to promote his interests. Greer also dropped a libel case against the Guardian.
Hamilton has admitted he accepted two payments totalling 10,000 pounds ($15,600) from Greer in the late 1980s, but has insisted that the money was paid to him for introducing clients to the lobbyist.

According to the Guardian, Greer also made payments to at least 23 other members of parliament or their local offices, of whom 20 are Conservatives. Some of the MPs concerned have said they gave no service, and were asked for none, in return.

The publicity over the Hamilton case has come at a bad time for Major who is preparing for a Conservative Party conference next week which he says "will be the launchpad for the next election campaign".
The Conservatives are more than 20 points behind the opposition Labour Party in the opinion polls with a general election due by May next year.
Labour leader Tony Blair on Wednesday called for an independent investigation into political donations in the light of the Guardian's claims about Greer's payments to MPs.

And in another attempt to embarrass Major, the leader of the minority Liberal Democrats, Paddy Ashdown, urged him to consider whether Hamilton should be allowed to remain as a Conservative MP. The Conservatives have a majority of just one in parliament.
Sixteen Conservative MPs resigned government posts in 1994 and 1995 over allegations of financial and sexual impropriety.

In a bid to defuse the sleaze issue, Major set up an independent inquiry into the standards of conduct in public life. As a result of its report, parliament earlier this year agreed much tougher rules about when legislators should publicly declare non-parliamentary earnings.
